voiceNote: Pace is roughly 150 words per minute. Keep claims to what the demo actually shows.

scenes.title: Enterprise Knowledge Assistant
scenes.text: This is the Enterprise Knowledge Assistant: a production-grade, retrieval-augmented generation app built with dot net nine, React, PostgreSQL with pgvector, Redis, and a large language model behind an interface. Ask questions about your company's documents, and get streamed answers with citations, with multi-tenancy, safety checks, cost controls, and observability built in.

scenes.title: Architecture
scenes.text: Here is the shape of it. The React app signs users in through OpenID Connect, then talks to a clean-architecture ASP dot net API. Postgres holds the data, the vectors, full-text search, and the ingestion queue. Redis handles rate limits, idempotency, locks, and a semantic cache. In this demo the answers come from an offline stand-in that quotes your documents. One setting switches it to Claude.

scenes.title: Sign in
scenes.text: Sign-in is handled by Keycloak using the authorization code flow with PKCE. Tokens are kept in memory, never in local storage. Alice is an admin, and her tenant is fully isolated from every other tenant.

scenes.title: Workspaces
scenes.text: Workspaces organize documents. Create one, search across them, and rename it. Updates use optimistic concurrency, so two people can't silently overwrite each other's changes.

scenes.title: Members and roles
scenes.text: Membership controls who can see a workspace. Alice adds Bob as an editor and Carol as a viewer. Anyone who isn't a member doesn't even learn the workspace exists. They get a not-found response, not a forbidden one.

scenes.title: Document ingestion
scenes.text: Now the documents. Upload Markdown or PDF files. Ingestion runs in the background through a Postgres-backed queue: extract the text, split it into chunks, embed them, and store them. Progress is pushed to the browser live over SignalR, so each file flips to ready as soon as it's searchable.

scenes.title: Managing documents
scenes.text: Documents can be searched, renamed, reprocessed, or deleted. Deletes are soft, and every one of these actions lands in the audit log.

scenes.title: Ask your documents
scenes.text: Now ask a question. The answer streams in over server-sent events, with numbered citations that link back to the sources. Retrieval is hybrid: vector search and full-text search, fused with reciprocal rank fusion, and permissions are enforced inside the SQL query itself, not after the fact.

scenes.title: Feedback and cache
scenes.text: Rate an answer with a thumbs up or down. Ask the same question again, and the semantic cache replies instantly, with no model call and no cost.

scenes.title: Safety
scenes.text: Safety is built into the pipeline. This security policy hides an instruction telling the model to reveal its system prompt. It is neutralized before the model ever sees it. Personal details like email addresses are masked, and the user is told. And when a question isn't covered by the documents, the assistant says so, instead of making something up.

scenes.title: Role-based access
scenes.text: Now signed in as Carol, a viewer. She can read and ask questions, but there are no upload, edit, or delete controls, and no operations or audit pages. The API enforces this too, not just the interface.

scenes.title: Tenant isolation
scenes.text: Dave is an admin too, but in a different tenant. He sees none of Alice's workspaces. Tenant filters are applied globally in the data layer and fail closed, so a missing tenant means no data.

scenes.title: Operations
scenes.text: Back as admin, the operations page shows what the system is doing: questions answered, latency percentiles, cost per question, tokens by model, outcomes, and the monthly quota for the tenant, which is enforced on every request. At the bottom are the latest evaluation scores, compared with the committed baseline.

scenes.title: Audit log
scenes.text: Every change is recorded: who did what, to which entity, and when.

scenes.title: Observability
scenes.text: Everything is instrumented with OpenTelemetry. Here is one chat request as a trace, with spans for the embedding, the retrieval, and the model stream, exported to the Aspire dashboard. Errors can also flow to Sentry, with sensitive headers scrubbed.

scenes.title: Quality
scenes.text: Under the hood: close to three hundred automated tests running against real Postgres and Redis, a golden-set evaluation suite that fails the build on a regression, a k6 load test, browser tests with Playwright, Docker images with a separate migrations step, a runbook, and a log of architecture decisions.

scenes.title: Get it
scenes.text: That's the Enterprise Knowledge Assistant. The code is open source on GitHub, and configuration for a free deployment on Render, Neon, and Auth0 is included. Thanks for watching.
